pairsWith.noteUz: Bu nazariya beti Coursebook 4-unit (Days to Remember) grammatikasini takrorlaydi: sifat va ravish, -ing/-ed sifatlar, Past Continuous shakli.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 4-UNIT NAZARIYA (20-bet, PDF 19). Yuqorida chapda ko'k '4', sarlavha: 'Adjectives - Adverbs - Past Continuous'. Och pushti ramka.

'Adjectives - Adverbs': • Adjectives describe nouns. 'We live in a small village.' • Adjectives ending in -ing (e.g. interesting, amazing, etc) are used to describe what somebody or something is like. 'The film was boring. She is a very interesting person.' • Adjectives ending in -ed (e.g. amazed, surprised, puzzled, etc) are used to describe how somebody feels. 'The children were terrified when they heard the thunder.' • Adverbs describe verbs, other adverbs or adjectives. 'He works hard. He runs very fast. She is extremely polite.' • Adverbs usually go after verbs. They can also go before verbs (adverbs of frequency). 'She spoke softly. He always drives carefully.'
'Form': • We usually form an adverb by adding -ly to the adjective. 'dangerous - dangerously' • When the adjective ends in -le we drop the -e and add -y. 'gentle - gently' • When the adjective ends in a consonant + y we drop the -y and add -ily. 'easy - easily' • When the adjective ends in -l we add -ly. 'wonderful - wonderfully' • Some adverbs have either a totally different form or the same form as the adjective. Study the table. JADVAL Adjective → Adverb: good → well; fast → fast; hard → hard; early → early; late → late.
'Note': The following words end in -ly but they are adjectives: friendly, lively, lonely, lovely, silly, ugly. 'He's a friendly person.'

'Past Continuous' JADVALI: Affirmative: I was eating, he/she/it was eating, we/you/they were eating. Interrogative: Was I eating? Was he/she/it eating? Were we/you/they eating? Negative - Long form: I was not eating, he/she/it was not eating, we/you/they were not eating. Short form: I wasn't eating, he/she/it wasn't eating, we/you/they weren't eating.
'Short answers': Was he/she/it ...? - Yes, he/she/it, etc was. No, he/she/it, etc wasn't. Were we/you/they ...? - Yes, we/I, etc were. No, we/I, etc weren't.

Bet raqami: pastda chapda '20'.

exercises.instructionEn: Adjectives describe nouns: We live in a small village. Adjectives ending in -ing (interesting, amazing) describe what somebody or something is like: The film was boring. She is a very interesting person. Adjectives ending in -ed (amazed, surprised, puzzled) describe how somebody feels: The children were terrified when they heard the thunder. Adverbs describe verbs, other adverbs or adjectives: He works hard. He runs very fast. She is extremely polite. Adverbs usually go after verbs. They can also go before verbs (adverbs of frequency): She spoke softly. He always drives carefully.
exercises.instructionUz: Sifatlar otlarni tasvirlaydi: Biz kichik qishloqda yashaymiz. -ing bilan tugaydigan sifatlar (interesting, amazing) kim/nima QANDAY ekanini bildiradi: Film zerikarli edi. U juda qiziqarli inson. -ed bilan tugaydigan sifatlar (amazed, surprised, puzzled) kim o'zini QANDAY HIS QILIShINI bildiradi: Bolalar momaqaldiroqni eshitib qo'rqib ketishdi. Ravishlar fe'l, boshqa ravish yoki sifatni tasvirlaydi: U qattiq ishlaydi. U juda tez yuguradi. U nihoyatda muloyim. Ravishlar odatda fe'ldan KEYIN keladi; chastota ravishlari fe'ldan OLDIN ham kelishi mumkin: U sekin gapirdi. U har doim ehtiyotkorlik bilan haydaydi.
exercises.explanationUz:
SIFAT va RAVISh - FARQI.

  SIFAT → OTni tasvirlaydi:
    a SMALL village
  RAVISh → FE'Lni (yoki sifat/
    ravishni) tasvirlaydi:
    He works HARD.
    He runs VERY fast.
    She is EXTREMELY polite.


-ING va -ED SIFATLAR:

  -ING = narsa QANDAY (sabab):
    The film was BORING.
    She is an INTERESTING person.
  -ED = odam QANDAY HIS QILADI
    (natija):
    The children were TERRIFIED.
    I'm BORED. (zerikdim)

  ⚠ 'I'm boring' = men zerikarli
  odamman! 'I'm bored' = zerikdim.


RAVISh O'RNI:

  Fe'ldan KEYIN: She spoke SOFTLY.
  Chastota ravishi fe'ldan OLDIN:
    He ALWAYS drives carefully.

points.en: We live in a small village. (adjectives describe nouns)
The film was boring. She is a very interesting person. (-ing: what somebody/something is like)

points.en: The children were terrified when they heard the thunder. (-ed: how somebody feels)
points.uz: Bolalar momaqaldiroqni eshitib qo'rqib ketishdi. (-ed: qanday his qiladi)

exercises.instructionEn: Form: We usually form an adverb by adding -ly to the adjective: dangerous - dangerously. When the adjective ends in -le we drop the -e and add -y: gentle - gently. When the adjective ends in a consonant + y we drop the -y and add -ily: easy - easily. When the adjective ends in -l we add -ly: wonderful - wonderfully. Some adverbs have either a totally different form or the same form as the adjective: good - well; fast - fast; hard - hard; early - early; late - late. Note: The following words end in -ly but they are adjectives: friendly, lively, lonely, lovely, silly, ugly. He's a friendly person.
exercises.instructionUz: Shakl: Ravish odatda sifatga -ly qo'shib yasaladi: dangerous - dangerously. Sifat -le bilan tugasa, -e tushib -y qo'shiladi: gentle - gently. Undosh + y bilan tugasa, -y tushib -ily qo'shiladi: easy - easily. -l bilan tugasa, -ly qo'shiladi: wonderful - wonderfully. Ba'zi ravishlar butunlay boshqa yoki sifat bilan bir xil shaklda: good - well; fast - fast; hard - hard; early - early; late - late. Eslatma: quyidagi so'zlar -ly bilan tugaydi, lekin SIFAT: friendly, lively, lonely, lovely, silly, ugly. U do'stona odam.
exercises.explanationUz:
RAVISh YASASh - SIFAT + -LY.

  1) ODDIY: + -ly
     dangerous → dangerousLY
     slow → slowly

  2) -LE: -e → -y
     gentle → gentLY
     terrible → terribly

  3) UNDOSh + Y: -y → -ily
     easy → easILY
     happy → happily

  4) -L: + -ly (ikkita l!)
     wonderful → wonderfulLY
     careful → carefully


MAXSUS ShAKLLAR:

  good → WELL (butunlay boshqa)
  fast → fast    (bir xil)
  hard → hard    (bir xil)
  early → early  (bir xil)
  late → late    (bir xil)

  ⚠ 'He runs fastly' ✗ → 'fast'.
  ⚠ 'hardly' = deyarli emas
  (boshqa ma'no!); 'lately' =
  yaqinda.


⚠ -LY BILAN TUGAYDIGAN SIFATLAR:

  friendly, lively, lonely, lovely,
  silly, ugly - bular RAVISh EMAS:
  He's a FRIENDLY person.

points.en: good → well; fast → fast; hard → hard; early → early; late → late
friendly, lively, lonely, lovely, silly, ugly = adjectives (He's a friendly person.)

exercises.instructionEn: Affirmative: I was eating, he/she/it was eating, we/you/they were eating. Interrogative: Was I eating? Was he/she/it eating? Were we/you/they eating? Negative: I was not (wasn't) eating, he/she/it was not (wasn't) eating, we/you/they were not (weren't) eating. Short answers: Was he/she/it ...? - Yes, he/she/it was. / No, he/she/it wasn't. Were we/you/they ...? - Yes, we/I were. / No, we/I weren't.
exercises.instructionUz: Tasdiq: I was eating, he/she/it was eating, we/you/they were eating. So'roq: Was I eating? Was he/she/it eating? Were we/you/they eating? Inkor: I was not (wasn't) eating, he/she/it was not (wasn't) eating, we/you/they were not (weren't) eating. Qisqa javob: Was he/she/it ...? - Yes, he/she/it was. / No, he/she/it wasn't. Were we/you/they ...? - Yes, we/I were. / No, we/I weren't.
exercises.explanationUz:
PAST CONTINUOUS = was / were +
  fe'l-ING.

  TASDIQ:
    I / he / she / it WAS eating
    we / you / they WERE eating

  SO'ROQ (was/were oldinga):
    WAS he eating?
    WERE they eating?

  INKOR:
    I WASN'T eating
    they WEREN'T eating

  QISQA JAVOB:
    Was he eating? - Yes, he WAS. /
    No, he WASN'T.
    Were they eating? - Yes, they
    WERE. / No, they WEREN'T.


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  'yeyayotgan edi' = was eating.
  O'tmishda MA'LUM PAYTDA davom
  etayotgan harakat.

  ⚠ Ishlatilishi keyingi betda
  (21-bet).

points.en: I / he / she / it was eating — we / you / they were eating
Was he eating? — Were they eating?
I wasn't eating — they weren't eating
Was he ...? — Yes, he was. / No, he wasn't. — Were they ...? — Yes, they were. / No, they weren't.
